architecture.mechanism: Real-time multi-sensor telemetry acquisition (sensors measuring vehicle parameters continuously) with data logged to a database and displayed live to the driver, enabling post-event analysis of parameter traces.
architecture.intervention: Mount a multi-parameter telemetry logger on the 2021 Chevrolet Equinox (accelerometers on the driveshaft, transmission tail housing, and floor pan; non-contact optical or magnetic RPM sensor on the driveshaft; wheel-speed sensors already present via ABS), record synchronized vibration amplitude, driveshaft RPM, and vehicle speed to an on-board memory card, and replay the time-series traces after the road test to identify which rotating component (driveshaft imbalance, tire uniformity, wheel bearing, or U-joint) produces the dominant 1×-revolutions-per-second forcing frequency relative to driveshaft RPM and road speed.
architecture.expected_effect: Pinpoint diagnosis of the vibration source at 67,000 miles without reliance on a MIL, allowing a targeted repair (driveshaft rebalance/replacement, tire match-mounting, or wheel-bearing replacement) that eliminates the shaking and wobbling reported across various speeds.
architecture.falsification_test: Drive the vehicle at the speed range reported by the owner; if the accelerometer frequency spectrum shows no dominant peak at the driveshaft 1×-rev frequency, no peak at tire 1×-rev frequency, and no broadband bearing race frequencies, then the telemetry-based diagnosis is invalidated and another root cause (e.g., body/chassis resonance excited by tire imbalance, engine mount, or brake rotor DTV) must be sought.
